author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: A booked visit can be corrected
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction replaces the booked visit rather than adding a second one, and the owner's record shows the result.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when the page that corrects it is opened, then the form already holds that visit's date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries them and the owner's record is shown.
Given a pet with one visit, when that visit is corrected, then the pet still has one visit.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the visit keeps what it had.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the visit keeps what it had.
Given an owner's record, when it is opened, then it offers no way to correct a visit.
Edge case 3: correcting a visit of a pet that does not belong to the named owner is refused, as booking it is.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
A link or button to the correction page from the owner's record — the page is reached by its address alone
Correcting anything about a visit beyond its date and description
notes: NG-5 narrowed by the owner at intake (line 1); recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowed.md, which amends the NG-5 half of the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR. Three open questions are recorded in the PRD rather than answered, per the owner's instruction to take the narrowest reading: whether an already-passed visit is correctable at all under the future-date rule, whether the correction page lists the pet's other visits, and how a correction is confirmed. Two follow-ups outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an Index row for the new ADR, and docs/system-design.md carries the mechanism for the correction route.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction route is the existing optional-path-variable lookup that PetController.findPet already demonstrates (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java:75-87, grep-resolved; IDE oracle not connected, so this is the weaker basis). VisitController's single @ModelAttribute("visit") method gains an optional visitId path variable: absent it builds a new Visit and adds it to the pet as today, present it resolves the pet's existing visit. Binding then writes onto that resolved instance and owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE through the Pet.visits @OneToMany(cascade=ALL) association, so the pet gains no second visit. The traversal owner -> pet -> visit is the aggregate shape docs/system-design.md #contracts already records under 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'; no VisitRepository is introduced. The identity lookup on Pet mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer), keeping collection scanning out of the controller. Recorded in docs/system-design.md #visit-correction; Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController now cite REQ-VIS-003.
integration_points: Entry point GET+POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit binds the resolved persisted Visit. Binding target: the existing @InitBinder disallow-list ('id', '*.id') on VisitController, which leaves date and description as the only bindable properties of Visit -- the same allow-surface the booking route already binds. No new bindable property is introduced.

Repository boundary: OwnerRepository. Double = framework stub (@MockitoBean), the reason being that OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository<Owner,Integer> and its inherited surface makes a hand-written double impractical; VisitControllerTests already establishes this stub. The Owner/Pet/Visit graph the stub returns is real, so 'the pet still has one visit' is asserted on the real aggregate, never on mock interactions.
Transport boundary: MockMvc, the project's one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy); it drives the real MVC dispatch, binding and validation.

Template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm reused unchanged: the form posts to the current URL (no th:action), and th:if="${visit['new']}" already branches the heading. The correction page therefore renders without correction-specific markup.

patterns.description: findPet: @PathVariable(name=..., required=false) Integer on a shared @ModelAttribute method serving both the create and the edit route -- the exact shape loadPetWithVisit adopts
getPet(Integer): identity lookup scanning the aggregate's own collection and returning null when absent -- the shape Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors
processNewVisitForm: the non-future-date rejection and the redirect:/owners/{ownerId} exit the correction POST reuses verbatim

risks.risk: Identifier tampering (IDOR) on the new visitId path variable: a visit belonging to another owner's pet could be corrected. Threat Model row 'Mass assignment / identifier tampering via form binding', docs/system-design.md #threat-model.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by traversing the named owner's named pet (docs/system-design.md #visit-correction). No global visit lookup exists -- there is no VisitRepository -- so a foreign identifier resolves to null and is refused on the same IllegalArgumentException path a foreign petId already takes. PRD edge case 3.

risks.risk: Correction route loads the full owner graph per request; it scales with one owner's pets and their visits.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form -- the single owners.findById the booking route already performs. Bounded by the eager-fetch decision in docs/system-design.md #persistence (open-in-view disabled). No new data-scaling path is added. See notes: the doc has no Scale and Load section to carry a row.

risks.risk: Adding correction-specific confirmation wording or a button label would introduce user-facing text needing all eleven message bundles.
risks.mitigation: Emit no flash message and add no message key (docs/system-design.md #visit-correction). REQ-VIS-003 requires only that the owner's record is shown; REQ-LANG-002 forbids hard-coded or partly translated wording.

risks.risk: Reusing the template makes the 'Previous Visits' table render on the correction page, since th:if="${!visit['new']}" is true for a persisted visit. That table lists the visit being corrected alongside the others.
risks.mitigation: Accepted under the narrowest reading: the owner directed template reuse, and no acceptance criterion speaks to the list. Recorded as PRD open question 'whether the correction page lists the pet's other visits'; the implementer changes no markup.

notes: Owner-instructed narrowest reading applied to three open choices; each stays an open question rather than a decision. (1) Confirmation: none emitted, owner record shown. (2) Other visits listed: whatever template reuse yields, no markup change. (3) Already-passed visit: the booking rules bind, so its date must move forward -- PRD edge case 4 and the ADR Consequences already state this; nothing extra is designed. Brief defect surfaced, not overridden: design-validation requires each data-scaling path to cite a docs/system-design.md Scale and Load row, but this project's design doc (harness 2026-07-31) has no such section. The correction route adds no new scaling path, so creating the section for this slice would exceed it; the load characteristic is recorded in the risks entry against the existing Persistence eager-fetch statement instead. Product follow-ups discharged: docs/adr/README.md Index gains the 2026-09-18 non-goal ADR row, and docs/system-design.md #visit-correction carries the mechanism. Design-doc writes are provenance-marked, since the document's global header claims bootstrap-survey derivation that a designed-ahead section would falsify. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log; autofix audit skipped.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Out of scope for this slice, noted once and not a reservation against this change: the pre-existing booking handler still binds the aggregate root with binding enabled -- VisitController.java:120 'public String processNewVisitForm(@ModelAttribute Owner owner, @PathVariable int petId, @Valid Visit visit,' -- and then saves that owner, so a stray request parameter such as firstName can write an Owner field on the booking POST. The correction route added here explicitly closes that hole (binding = false) and documents why, so the two routes now differ. A follow-up slice could align the booking route; changing it here would alter behavior on a route REQ-VIS-003's bullets do not name.
approved_aspects: IDOR on the new visitId path variable is structurally prevented, not merely checked. VisitController.loadPetWithVisit resolves the visit only by owner -> pet -> visit (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/VisitController.java:76 'Pet pet = owner.getPet(petId);' and :90 'Visit visit = pet.getVisit(visitId);'), and no global visit lookup exists to bypass it: 'grep -rn VisitRepository src/ docs/' returns no hit under src/ (only docs/system-design.md:16 and docs/adr/2026-07-31-relational-persistence-with-spring-data-jpa.md:23, both stating its absence). A foreign visitId therefore resolves to null and is refused at :91-93. This satisfies the 'Trusting cross-request state' row of docs/security-principles.md: the correction POST re-resolves the aggregate on every request rather than trusting the identifier a prior GET validated.

Mass assignment (docs/security-principles.md 'Mass assignment' row) is closed on both new routes. The class-level @InitBinder at VisitController.java:55 'dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");' applies to the new GET and POST handlers, and Visit declares only date and description as bindable properties (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/Visit.java:40 'private LocalDate date;' and :43 'private String description;'), so the bound surface equals the form surface. The correction POST additionally binds the aggregate root with binding switched off -- VisitController.java:142 'public String processVisitCorrectionForm(@ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner, @Valid Visit visit,' -- so no request parameter can write an Owner field on the path to owners.save(owner). @Valid is present on the bound Visit on the persisting path, meeting the 'every request-bound object that reaches a save carries @Valid' item.

No new injection, output-escaping, or resource surface is introduced. The template is reused unchanged and renders every request-derived value through th:text (src/main/resources/templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:24 '' and :52 ''), so Thymeleaf default escaping stays on. A sweep of src/main/java for 'Runtime', 'ProcessBuilder', '.exec(', 'FileWriter', 'FileOutputStream', '/tmp/', 'enableDefaultTyping', 'JsonTypeInfo' returned no production hit beyond unrelated AOT RuntimeHints imports and CrashController's deliberate RuntimeException. Data access stays on the derived query OwnerRepository.findById (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerRepository.java:60 'Optional findById(Integer id);'); no concatenated query text is added.

The new exception message carries no sensitive value into the error page. VisitController.java:92-93 builds 'Visit with id ' + visitId + ' not found for pet with id ' + petId + '.' from two path variables that Spring has already parsed as Integer, so a non-numeric value never reaches the string, and src/main/resources/templates/error.html:19 '

Exception message

' escapes what it renders. This meets the 'Secret disclosure through logs and errors' row; the error page's habit of rendering the exception message is the recorded baseline (docs/prd.md REQ-SYS-002 open defect), which this change does not widen. No credential-shaped string appears in the diff: a read of the full change set found no token, password, secret, or key literal.

Supply chain unchanged and not independently scanned. build.gradle is not in the change set ('python3 scripts/changeset.py --name-only' lists no build file), so no dependency was added, removed, or version-bumped. Versions read from build.gradle:5 "id 'org.springframework.boot' version '4.1.1'"; no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in this build and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran in this review -- that check is not run, not clean.

Concurrency and shared state are safe: the only field added to the singleton controller is the immutable constant VisitController.java:45 'private static final String VIEWS_VISIT_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM = "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm";', and Pet.getVisit (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/Pet.java:90-97) reads only the receiver's own collection. No check anywhere in the diff was removed or weakened -- the extracted rejectVisitDateNotInFuture helper (VisitController.java:155-159) preserves the booking route's non-future-date rejection verbatim and applies the same rule to the correction route.
